sources.entry: AdGuard for Safari - The most advanced ad blocking extension for Safari

summary.one_liner: AdGuard's open-source ad blocking extension for Safari on macOS, now branded AdGuard Mini (formerly AdGuard for Safari).
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a free, open-source Safari extension that blocks banners, video ads, popups, autoplay videos and overlays, and blocks trackers and analytics beacons. It also removes annoyances such as cookie notices, social widgets and sticky bars. Users control it from the Safari toolbar, can pause protection, allowlist sites, and block page elements manually. It supports popular filter lists, custom filters, and an advanced rule editor. The README says advanced features (system-wide protection, real-time filter updates, AdGuard Extra for anti-adblock scripts, advanced custom filters) require an AdGuard Ad Blocker license or in-app purchase. It also points users to the full AdGuard for Mac app as a more effective alternative.
use_cases: block ads in Safari on Mac
stop trackers and analytics in Safari
report missed ads or false positives
how_to_run: Install AdGuard Mini (formerly AdGuard for Safari) as a Safari extension, as described in the README's project links
Enable the extension in Safari settings and choose filter lists from the Safari toolbar menu
For developer setup, see DEVELOPMENT.md referenced in the README
stack: TestFlight (for beta testing of AdGuard Mini for Mac)
notable: Open source and free, with the same codebase now marketed as AdGuard Mini
Element picker for blocking any element manually on a page
Controls from the Safari toolbar, including pause and allowlist
Optional advanced features unlocked by an AdGuard license or in-app purchase
Points to AdGuard for Mac for system-wide blocking beyond Safari
caveats: Advanced features require a paid AdGuard Ad Blocker license or in-app purchase
Safari extension is limited by browser API restrictions; the README says the full AdGuard for Mac app filters better and has no rule limit
Works only in Safari on macOS, per the README's context
